origin.description: Newton-Raphson steady state with a full or banded difference Jacobian.
origin.usage: stode(y, time = 0, func, parms = NULL, rtol = 1e-6, atol = 1e-8, ctol = 1e-8, ...)

arguments.name: y
arguments.text: Initial state. Names are kept when y is a dict.

arguments.name: func
arguments.text: func(time, state, parms) returns a list whose first element is the derivatives.

arguments.name: parms
arguments.text: Passed through to func. NULL when the model has no parameters.

origin.details: The step is the solution of J delta = -f. The perturbation added to a state is max(abs(y) * 1e-8, 1e-8). A banded Jacobian perturbs every (bandup + banddown + 1)th unknown together.
origin.value: A list with y, and attributes precis and steady.
origin.example:
fun <- function(t, y, p) list(c(-0.1 * y[1] + 0.02 * y[2], 0.1 * y[1] - 0.2 * y[2]))
stode(y = c(1, 1), func = fun)

translation.description: Newton-Raphson steady state with a full or banded difference Jacobian.
translation.usage: stode(y, times=0, func=None, parms=None, rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-8, ctol=1e-8, **kwargs)

arguments.name: y
arguments.text: Initial state. Names are kept when y is a dict.

arguments.name: func
arguments.text: func(time, state, parms) returns a list whose first element is the derivatives.

arguments.name: parms
arguments.text: Passed through to func. NULL when the model has no parameters.

translation.details: The step is the solution of J delta = -f. The perturbation added to a state is max(abs(y) * 1e-8, 1e-8). A banded Jacobian perturbs every (bandup + banddown + 1)th unknown together.
translation.value: A list with y, and attributes precis and steady.
translation.example:
from rootSolve import stode

def fun(t, y, p):
    return [[-0.1 * y[0] + 0.02 * y[1], 0.1 * y[0] - 0.2 * y[1]]]

print(stode([1.0, 1.0], func=fun))
